minutes.headline: Trust Fund Commission voted unanimously to adopt nine governing documents, including the resident guide, operational manual and investment policy.
minutes.summary: The chair walked through the new resident guide for applying to town trust funds, the operational manual and application forms. The two members present then adopted all nine documents in one motion. The chair also reported on the Select Board declining the warrant article, the unanswered charter question, the pending Attorney General review and a dispute with the school department over trust fund records.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none in the room or on Zoom. A member commended the chair's recent work. Public comment was again declared absent at the end of the meeting.

votes.motion: Accept nine documents as written: risk mitigation and best practices policy, investment policy statement, Select Board quick guide, operational manual, resident guide, trust fund application, scholarship and school trust application, resident checklist, and form TC4 (scholarship and school award presentation)

budget_items.topic: Income eligibility for residents in financial need funds
budget_items.what_was_said: Eligibility is set at a multiple of the federal poverty guideline, with figures varying by household size. The chair gave examples of household incomes that would qualify.
The Attorney General's administrative cy pres review applies to funds under a size threshold and over a certain age.

budget_items.topic: Payments to businesses and invoice-based awards
budget_items.what_was_said: The town pays the business directly rather than the applicant. Awards can top up other grants for projects such as a ramp.
Applicants with cash savings above a few months of fixed household bills are expected to use that first.

budget_items.topic: Investment management and bonding of trust funds
budget_items.what_was_said: Trust money is invested through an outside firm and the treasurer's bond covers it. The chair said the board would need its own bond if it took over investment.
The chair said some funds held through the school lost money last year and argued they are not being invested prudently.

decisions.decision: Language for the pre-filing form for the Attorney General review is still awaited from the town manager. The board will vote on it once received, then send it to the Attorney General, a process of about six weeks.
The trust fund matter will not be put into the special town meeting warrant. The advertisement is still to be drafted and ratified.
Approval of the September 10 minutes and the December 18 minutes was put off to the next meeting.
Next meeting set for November 11, 2026, in the regular second and fourth Wednesday cycle.
The school department letter will be discussed in detail at the next meeting. The school has been given time to respond, and the next step is asking the Select Board to enforce the request.
The review of the risk management policy and the Select Board continuity guide was deferred to the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The Trust Fund Commission voted unanimously, by voice vote of the two members present, to adopt nine governing documents in a single motion.
The nine include the resident guide, operational manual, investment policy statement, risk mitigation policy, application forms and a resident checklist.
The chair reported the trust fund matter will not go into the special town meeting warrant; the advertisement is still to be drafted and ratified.
The commission is still waiting on pre-filing form language from the town manager before a vote and a roughly six-week Attorney General review.
The school department records dispute was not resolved; the next step is asking the Select Board to enforce the request, with discussion set for the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The adopted resident guide and forms set out how residents apply for town trust fund money, including income eligibility, savings expectations and payment directly to businesses.
With the warrant article off the special town meeting, any change to how trust funds are governed or invested waits on the Attorney General review and a later vote.
